questions.question: The ionic radius of Al3+ is smaller than that of N3-. This is because Al3+ has: A fewer protons but more electrons than N3-; B more protons but fewer electrons than N3-; C more protons than N3- but the same number of electrons as N3-; D the same number of protons as N3- but fewer electrons.
steps: Al3+ has 13 protons and 10 electrons; N3- has 7 protons and 10 electrons.
Both ions are isoelectronic (10 electrons), so the difference is nuclear charge.
Al3+ has more protons, so it pulls its electrons in more strongly and has a smaller radius.

questions.question: Which diagram best represents the electron density map of a hydrogen chloride molecule? (The diagram options are shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: C: contours around both nuclei, closer together and more numerous round the larger Cl nucleus
steps: HCl is a polar covalent molecule, so the shared pair of electrons lies between the nuclei and the outer contour lines enclose both atoms.
Chlorine is more electronegative, so the electron density is greater and the contours are more crowded round the Cl nucleus than round H.
A and B show separate, unconnected contours (ions with no shared density), and D shows an almost symmetrical sharing, as in a non-polar molecule.

questions.topic: Dot And Cross Diagram Magnesium Chloride
questions.question: Which is the dot-and-cross diagram for magnesium chloride, showing only outer shell electrons? (The diagram options are shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: D: Mg2+ with 8 outer electrons in square brackets, flanked by two [Cl]- ions each with 8 electrons
steps: Magnesium chloride is ionic, MgCl2: Mg loses its 2 outer electrons and each of two Cl atoms gains one.
Mg2+ has the electronic structure 2,8 and is drawn with 8 electrons in square brackets and a 2+ charge; each Cl- has a full outer shell of 8 electrons and a 1- charge.
A and B show shared (covalent) electrons, and C shows Mg+ and one Cl-, which gives the wrong formula.

questions.question: Which ion has the greatest polarising power? A Cl-, B Mg2+, C Na+, D S2-.
steps: Polarising power is highest for a small, highly charged cation.
Mg2+ is small (for a 2+ ion) and has a 2+ charge, giving high charge density.
Cl- and S2- are anions, and Na+ is a smaller charge than Mg2+ with a larger radius.

questions.question: Some ionic radii are shown (shown in the figure below). Which compound has the strongest ionic bonding? A sodium fluoride; B sodium chloride; C potassium fluoride; D potassium chloride.
steps: Stronger ionic bonding comes from smaller ions with higher charge, giving a stronger attraction.
Of these ions, Na+ and F- are the smallest, so NaF has the strongest attraction.
Chloride and potassium ions are larger, giving weaker bonding.

questions.question: In which pair are the ions isoelectronic? A Ca2+ and S2-; B K+ and Br-; C Li+ and F-; D Mg2+ and Cl-.
steps: Ca2+ has 20 - 2 = 18 electrons; S2- has 16 + 2 = 18 electrons.
K+ (18) and Br- (36) differ; Li+ (2) and F- (10) differ; Mg2+ (10) and Cl- (18) differ.

questions.question: Which pair of ions gives the strongest ionic bonding? A Na+ and F-; B K+ and Br-; C Mg2+ and O2-; D Ca2+ and S2-.
steps: Strongest ionic bonding needs high charges and small ions.
Mg2+ and O2- both have high charges (2+ and 2-), and both are small ions.
The other pairs have either lower charges or larger ions (for example Ca2+ and S2- are larger).

questions.question: Which statement is not true for sodium chloride? A conducts electricity in aqueous solution; B conducts electricity when molten; C has a molecular structure; D has a giant structure.
questions.answer: C (sodium chloride has a molecular structure)
steps: Sodium chloride is an ionic compound with a giant ionic lattice, so D is true.
Ions are free to move when molten or dissolved, so A and B are true.
It does not have discrete molecules, so C is the false statement.

questions.question: Which pair of ions will form the compound with the most covalent character? A Li+ and I-; B Na+ and Br-; C K+ and Cl-; D Rb+ and F-.
steps: Covalent character increases when a small, highly charged cation polarises a large, easily distorted anion.
Li+ is the smallest cation here, and I- is the largest and most polarisable anion.
So Li+ and I- give the most covalent character.

questions.question: Which of these ions has the smallest ionic radius? A Al3+; B Ga3+; C Mg2+; D F-.
steps: Al3+ has 10 electrons and 13 protons, giving a small radius (about 54 pm).
Ga3+ has more electron shells (3d10 inner shell), so it is larger than Al3+.
Mg2+ and F- have 10 electrons with lower nuclear charge, so they are larger than Al3+.

questions.question: Which of these ions has the greatest ionic radius? A N3-; B F-; C Na+; D Al3+.
steps: All four ions have 10 electrons (isoelectronic).
Radius decreases as nuclear charge increases: N3- (7 protons) is the largest, then F-, Na+, Al3+.
So N3- has the greatest radius.

questions.question: A p-block element in Period 3 reacts to form an ionic compound. What could be the electronic configuration of the ion formed? A 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2; B 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6; C 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10; D 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 3d10 4s2 4p6.
steps: A p-block Period 3 element (such as Cl or S) forms an anion by gaining electrons into 3p.
Cl- or S2- gives 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6.
A is Mg2+ (s-block), and C and D involve 3d or 4p, which do not fit a Period 3 p-block ion.

questions.question: Which ion is the most polarisable? A Mg2+; B Ca2+; C Cl-; D I-.
steps: Polarisability is greatest for large anions with many electrons and a diffuse electron cloud.
I- is the largest ion here, so its electron cloud is most easily distorted.
The cations are small and highly charged, so they are least polarisable.

questions.question: Which of these ions has the greatest polarising power? A S2-; B Cl-; C K+; D Ca2+.
steps: Polarising power is a property of cations: small size and high charge.
Ca2+ is a small 2+ ion, with higher charge density than K+.
S2- and Cl- are anions and do not polarise other ions in this sense.

questions.question: Which of these isoelectronic ions has the largest radius? A Na+; B Mg2+; C O2-; D F-.
steps: All four ions have 10 electrons.
Radius increases as the number of protons decreases, since nuclear attraction on the same 10 electrons is weaker.
Protons: O2- 8, F- 9, Na+ 11, Mg2+ 12.
O2- has the fewest protons, so it has the largest radius.

questions.question: In which series are the ions in order of decreasing ionic radius? A Al3+ > Mg2+ > Na+; B Li+ > Na+ > K+; C N3- > O2- > F-; D O2- > S2- > Se2-.
steps: N3-, O2- and F- are isoelectronic (10 electrons), with 7, 8 and 9 protons.
Radius decreases as nuclear charge increases, so N3- > O2- > F-.
A and B are reversed, and D is in increasing radius down a group (S2- and Se2- are larger than O2-).

questions.question: Which properties of an anion result in it being most easily polarised? A large radius and large charge; B large radius and small charge; C small radius and small charge; D small radius and large charge.
steps: An anion is polarised when its electron cloud is distorted by a cation.
A large radius means outer electrons are far from the nucleus and easily distorted.
A large negative charge increases electron-electron repulsion, so the electron cloud is more easily distorted.

questions.question: A drop of aqueous copper(II) chromate(VI) is placed on damp filter paper connected to a DC supply. What is observed after a few minutes? A green colour moved to negative end; B green colour moved to positive end; C yellow colour moved to positive end and blue colour to negative end; D blue colour moved to positive end and yellow colour to negative end.
questions.answer: C (yellow chromate to positive end, blue Cu2+ to negative end)
steps: Copper(II) ions are positive (Cu2+) and move to the negative electrode, giving a blue colour there.
Chromate(VI) ions are negative (CrO4 2-) and are yellow, so they move to the positive electrode.
So the yellow colour moves to the positive end and the blue colour to the negative end (option C).

questions.question: Write an equation, including state symbols, for the third ionisation energy of barium.
steps: The third IE removes one electron from Ba2+(g).
Products are Ba3+(g) and one electron, with gaseous species.

questions.topic: Evidence Of Group 2 From Ionisation Energies
questions.question: State how the graph of the first eight ionisation energies of barium confirms that barium is in Group 2.
questions.answer: There is a large jump in ionisation energy after the second electron is removed, showing barium has two outer electrons.
steps: The first two ionisation energies are relatively low.
The third ionisation energy is much larger, because the next electron comes from a full inner shell.
A large jump after 2 electrons confirms 2 outer electrons, so Group 2.

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram for barium chloride, showing outer electrons only.
questions.answer: Ba2+ with no outer electrons, and two Cl- ions each with a complete octet (8 electrons), with the two electrons from Ba transferred to the two Cl atoms.
steps: Barium (2 outer electrons) transfers both outer electrons, one to each chlorine.
Ba becomes Ba2+ with no outer electrons, shown in square brackets with 2+ charge.
Each Cl gains one electron and becomes Cl- with 8 outer electrons, shown in square brackets with a 1- charge.

questions.topic: Mass Of Barium Chloride From Concentration
questions.question: Calculate the mass of barium chloride needed to form 150 cm3 of BaCl2(aq) with concentration 0.200 mol dm-3. Ar: Ba 137.3, Cl 35.5.
Write the ionic equation for the reaction of hydrochloric acid with carbonate ions. State symbols are not required.
steps: Carbonate ions react with hydrogen ions from the acid.
They form carbon dioxide and water.
Charges balance: left 2- + 2+ = 0, and the products are neutral.

questions.question: Give a reason why solid barium chloride does not conduct electricity.
questions.answer: The ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move to carry the charge.
steps: Electrical conduction needs charged particles that are free to move.
In the solid, the Ba2+ and Cl- ions are fixed in a giant lattice.
Ions only move when molten or dissolved.

questions.question: Which properties of a cation result in the greatest polarising power? A large radius and large charge; B large radius and small charge; C small radius and small charge; D small radius and large charge.
steps: Polarising power depends on charge density, charge divided by volume.
A small radius and large charge gives the highest charge density.
This maximises the distortion of the anion's electron cloud.

questions.question: Which row in the table shows the correct forces in a crystal of lithium iodide? (The table is shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: D: attractive forces, repulsive forces and some covalent character all present
steps: A crystal of an ionic compound has attractive forces between oppositely charged ions and repulsive forces between ions of the same charge; the attractions outweigh the repulsions overall.
Li+ is small with a high charge density, so it polarises the large, easily distorted I- ion, which gives the bonding some covalent character.
So all three columns are ticked.

questions.question: Which of these isoelectronic ions has the smallest ionic radius? A N3-; B F-; C Na+; D Al3+.
steps: All four ions have 10 electrons.
Radius falls as nuclear charge increases: N3- (7), F- (9), Na+ (11), Al3+ (13).
Al3+ with 13 protons has the strongest attraction on its electrons, so it is smallest.

questions.question: Which of these compounds would you expect to have the highest melting temperature? A NaCl; B NaF; C KCl; D KF.
steps: Higher melting temperature needs stronger ionic lattice, so high charge and small ions.
All four have 1+ and 1- ions, so the size of the ions decides.
Na+ and F- are the smallest ions here, giving the strongest attraction and highest melting temperature.

questions.question: Element X is in Group 2 and element Y is in Group 7. What is the formula of the compound formed? A XY; B X2Y; C XY2; D X2Y2.
steps: X is in Group 2, so it forms X2+.
Y is in Group 7, so it forms Y-.
Two Y- ions balance one X2+ ion, giving XY2.

questions.question: Under what conditions does the compound formed from X and Y conduct electricity? A solid, liquid and aqueous; B solid and aqueous only; C solid and liquid only; D liquid and aqueous only.
steps: Ionic compounds conduct when their ions are free to move.
In the solid state the ions are fixed in a lattice, so no conduction.
When molten or dissolved in water, the ions can move, so conduction occurs.

questions.question: Which has the smallest ionic radius? A F-; B Mg2+; C Na+; D O2-.
steps: F-, Mg2+, Na+ and O2- all have 10 electrons (isoelectronic).
Radius decreases as nuclear charge increases: O2- (8), F- (9), Na+ (11), Mg2+ (12).
Mg2+ has the most protons, so it is the smallest.

questions.question: A direct current is passed through a green solution of copper(II) chromate(VI). Which colours would be seen at each electrode after several minutes? (The options are shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: Blue at the negative electrode (Cu2+ ions); yellow at the positive electrode (chromate ions)
steps: Cu2+ ions are blue and positive, so they move towards the negative electrode.
Chromate(VI) ions, CrO4 2-, are yellow and negative, so they move to the positive electrode.
So blue collects at the negative electrode and yellow at the positive electrode.

questions.topic: Smallest Number Of Ions In Solution
questions.question: Which solution contains the smallest number of ions? A 500 cm3 of 0.06 mol dm-3 Ca(NO3)2; B 500 cm3 of 0.09 mol dm-3 KI; C 250 cm3 of 0.12 mol dm-3 BaCl2; D 250 cm3 of 0.09 mol dm-3 (NH4)2SO4.
steps: A: 0.030 mol Ca(NO3)2 x 3 ions = 0.090 mol ions.
B: 0.045 mol KI x 2 ions = 0.090 mol ions.
C: 0.030 mol BaCl2 x 3 ions = 0.090 mol ions.
D: 0.0225 mol (NH4)2SO4 x 3 ions (2 NH4+ and SO4 2-) = 0.0675 mol ions, the smallest number.

questions.question: Which compound has the greatest covalent character? A MgBr2; B MgF2; C NaBr; D NaF.
steps: Covalent character is greatest with a small, highly charged cation and a large anion.
Mg2+ is more highly charged and polarising than Na+, and Br- is larger and more polarisable than F-.
So MgBr2 has the greatest covalent character.

questions.question: Which combination of ions would be expected to form the compound with the highest melting temperature? A Li+ and Br-; B Mg2+ and O2-; C Sr2+ and S2-; D Rb+ and Cl-.
steps: Highest melting temperature needs the highest charges and smallest ions (strongest lattice).
Mg2+ and O2- both have 2+ and 2- charges and are small ions.
Sr2+ and S2- have higher charges but larger ions; Li+ and Rb+ compounds have 1+ ions.

questions.question: A piece of filter paper soaked in water has green copper(II) chromate(VI) crystals placed in the centre and is connected to a 20 V DC supply. What colours are observed on the paper after a few minutes? (The options are shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: Blue towards the negative electrode and yellow towards the positive electrode
steps: Cu2+ ions (blue) are positive and migrate to the negative electrode.
Chromate(VI) ions (yellow) are negative and migrate to the positive electrode.
So a blue band forms near the negative end and a yellow band near the positive end.

questions.question: Plot a graph of the ionic radii data for the ions of successive elements (the data table is shown in the figure below).
questions.answer: Graph of ionic radius / pm (y-axis) against ion (x-axis, N3- to Al3+ with a gap for Ne) with a straight line of best fit falling from 171 pm at N3- to 54 pm at Al3+
steps: Put the ions in order along the x-axis: N3-, O2-, F-, (Ne, left empty as it forms no ion), Na+, Mg2+, Al3+, evenly spaced; label the axes with units.
Choose a y-scale from 0 to 200 pm (25 pm per large square) so the points fill most of the grid.
Plot the five known points: N3- 171, O2- 140, F- 133, Na+ 102 and Al3+ 54 pm (Mg2+ is not plotted; it is to be predicted).
Draw one straight line of best fit with a negative gradient (about -18 pm per step) passing close to all the points.

questions.question: Predict the radius of the magnesium ion using a straight line of best fit on your graph.
steps: Read the radius at the Mg2+ position (between Na+ and Al3+) on the straight line of best fit.
The line gives about 76 pm; a hand-drawn line through the points gives a value of about 75 pm.
The value must be marked on the graph with construction lines.

questions.topic: Trend In Ionic Radii Nitride To Aluminium
questions.question: Explain the trend in the ionic radii from the nitride ion to the aluminium ion.
questions.answer: The ions N3-, O2-, F-, Na+, Mg2+ and Al3+ are isoelectronic (10 electrons), so the radius decreases as the number of protons increases, which pulls the same electrons more strongly.
steps: All these ions have 10 electrons, so electron-electron repulsion is the same across the series.
Going from N3- to Al3+, the number of protons increases from 7 to 13.
Greater nuclear charge attracts the electrons more strongly, so the ionic radius decreases.

questions.question: State the structure and bonding of sodium fluoride.
questions.answer: A giant ionic lattice of Na+ and F- ions held together by strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions (ionic bonding).
steps: Sodium fluoride is an ionic compound.
It has a regular giant lattice of alternating Na+ and F- ions.
The bonding is strong electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions.

questions.question: Explain how the electrical conductivity of sodium fluoride provides evidence for the existence of ions.
questions.answer: Solid NaF does not conduct because its ions are fixed in the lattice, but it conducts when molten or dissolved because the ions are then free to move and carry charge.
steps: Conduction needs charged particles that can move freely.
In the solid, the Na+ and F- ions are fixed in the lattice, so it does not conduct.
When molten or in solution, the ions are free to move towards the electrodes, showing that charged ions are present.

questions.question: Explain why the fluoride ion is difficult to polarise.
questions.answer: F- is small, so its outer electrons are close to a relatively high nuclear charge and held tightly, making the electron cloud hard to distort.
steps: Polarisation of an anion depends on how easily its electron cloud can be distorted.
F- is a small ion with only two shells, so its outer electrons are close to the nucleus.
The electrons are held tightly by the nucleus, so the cloud is hard to distort.

keywords: elements R T U V W X Y Z
questions.question: An outline of part of the Periodic Table is shown with letters that are not element symbols. Which elements are in the s-block? A R and U; B T and Y; C V and W; D X and Z. (The table outline is shown in the figure below.)
steps: R is in Group 1 (Period 2) and U is in Group 2 (Period 3), so both fill an s subshell.
T, V, W and Y are in Groups 6, 4, 7 and 6 respectively (p-block), and X and Z are in the d-block.

questions.topic: Element With Four Shells And Six Outer Electrons
questions.question: Which element has four occupied quantum shells, with six electrons in the outermost shell? A V; B X; C Y; D Z. (The table outline is shown in the figure below.)
steps: Four occupied shells means the element is in Period 4, and six outer electrons means Group 6 (16).
Y is in the fourth row, in Group 16 (selenium, 2,8,18,6); V and W are in Period 3, X is in Period 4 but in the d-block with 2 outer electrons, and Z is in Period 5.

questions.question: In which pair do the ions have the same electronic configuration? A R+ and T2-; B T2- and Y2-; C U2+ and T2-; D U2+ and W-. (The table outline is shown in the figure below.)
steps: U2+ is Mg2+ and T2- is O2-, which both have the configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6.
R+ (Li+, 1s2) differs from T2-, Y2- is Se2- (2,8,18,8) differs from T2-, and W- is Cl- (2,8,8) differs from Mg2+ (2,8).

questions.question: The first ionisation energies of four successive elements P, Q, R and S are shown (data shown in the figure below). Which element has atoms with a full outer shell of electrons? A P; B Q; C R; D S.
steps: The four elements are consecutive: P (1251) and Q (1521) have high first ionisation energies, then R (419) is far lower, so R is a Group 1 metal after Q.
So Q is a noble gas (argon, 1521) with a full outer shell, R is potassium and S is calcium, and P is chlorine.

questions.question: Which element could be X in a gaseous covalent compound with the formula HX? A P; B Q; C R; D S. (The first ionisation energy data are shown in the figure below.)
steps: P is chlorine (1251 kJ mol^-1), just before the noble gas Q.
A halogen forms the gaseous covalent hydride HX (HCl) by sharing one pair of electrons.

questions.question: Which element could be Y in an ionic compound with the formula YF2? A P; B Q; C R; D S. (The first ionisation energy data are shown in the figure below.)
steps: S is calcium, a Group 2 metal with first ionisation energy 590 kJ mol^-1 after the Group 1 metal R (419).
Calcium loses 2 electrons to form Ca2+, which combines with two F- ions as the ionic compound CaF2.

questions.question: Which element has atoms with the largest atomic radius? A P; B Q; C R; D S. (The first ionisation energy data are shown in the figure below.)
steps: R (419 kJ mol^-1) is the Group 1 metal, potassium, which has the lowest first ionisation energy.
P (Cl) and Q (Ar) are in Period 3 with three shells, whereas R (K) and S (Ca) are in Period 4 with four shells.
K has one proton fewer than Ca in the same shell, so its outer electron is pulled in less strongly and its atom is the largest.

questions.question: Which compound shows the greatest degree of polarisation? A sodium chloride; B sodium iodide; C magnesium chloride; D magnesium iodide.
steps: Greatest polarisation needs a small, highly charged cation and a large, polarisable anion.
Mg2+ is more highly charged than Na+, and I- is larger than Cl-.
So magnesium iodide is the most polarised.

questions.question: The isoelectronic ions N3-, O2-, F-, Na+, Mg2+ and Al3+ are considered. Which is shown in order of decreasing ionic radius? A Na+ > Mg2+ > Al3+; B Mg2+ > Na+ > Al3+; C Al3+ > Na+ > Mg2+; D Al3+ > Mg2+ > Na+.
steps: All six ions have 10 electrons.
Radius decreases as nuclear charge rises: Na+ (11) > Mg2+ (12) > Al3+ (13) in protons.
So A is in decreasing radius order.

questions.question: Which ions are shown in order of increasing ionic radius? A F- > O2- > N3-; B F- > N3- > O2-; C O2- > N3- > F-; D N3- > O2- > F-.
questions.answer: A: F-, O2-, N3- (ionic radii 133 < 140 < 171 pm)
steps: The ions are isoelectronic (10 electrons), so the radius increases as the number of protons falls: F- (9 protons) < O2- (8) < N3- (7).
Option A lists the ions in increasing radius order, with F- smallest.
The options are printed with ">" signs; if read literally as "greater than", D would be true, but that is the decreasing order and does not match the question wording.

questions.question: Which ion is isoelectronic with a noble gas atom (Group 0)? A H+; B O-; C Sc3+; D Zn2+.
steps: Sc has 21 electrons, so Sc3+ has 18 electrons, the same as argon.
H+ has 0 electrons, O- has 9 and Zn2+ has 28.
Only Sc3+ matches a noble gas (Ar).

questions.question: Which species are arranged in order of increasing radius? A K+ < Ar < Cl- < Br-; B Cl- < Ar < K+ < Br-; C Br- < Cl- < Ar < K+; D Cl- < Br- < Ar < K+.
steps: K+, Ar and Cl- are isoelectronic (18 electrons).
Among them, radius increases as nuclear charge decreases: K+ (19) < Ar (18) < Cl- (17).
Br- has the largest radius (extra shell), so the order is K+ < Ar < Cl- < Br-.

questions.question: Which cation would be the most polarising? Options: A small radius, large charge; B small radius, small charge; C large radius, small charge; D large radius, large charge.
steps: Polarising power is highest for the highest charge density (charge over size).
Small radius and large charge gives the greatest charge density.
So option A is the most polarising cation.
